newsitem.title: FRANCE: Synthelabo sees Europe competition rising.
newsitem.headline: Synthelabo sees Europe competition rising.

text.p: Pharmaceuticals firm Synthelabo aims to sharply increase sales by the year 2000 but expects profitability growth to slow due to rising competition, chairman Herve Guerin said on Tuesday.

Synthelabo, 57 percent controlled by cosmetics giant L'Oreal, aims to take three percent of the market with sales of between 18 and 20 billion francs ($3.5 billion) by the year 2000, up from two percent currently with 1996 sales of 10.4 billion.
"I think it's possible for Synthelabo to become the leading independent company (in the sector) in Europe," Guerin told an analysts' meeting.
But he said earnings per share growth would average 15-20 percent annually compared with 25 percent over the past eight years, because of heightened competition in the field.
Guerin said roughly half the sales growth anticipated by the year 2000 should be generated by acquisitions in Europe.

The group has formed alliances with Japanese and U.S. drug firms. It has a joint venture, Lorex Pharmaceutical, with Searle, a unit of Monsanto Co, in the United States and a Japanese venture with Fujisawa.
Synthelabo's research and development spending should rise in absolute terms, while remaining around 15 percent of sales, he said. It expects to register eight new molecules by 2001.
